analysis:
This PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the Last-updated date (line 3) and rewrites the forced tool_choice section (head hunk ~2017-2040). No executable code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, authorization or cache-storage logic is changed, so no concrete security regression is observable in the supplied evidence.

The new text describes coordinator routing of required/named tool_choice requests only to builds listed in `tool_constraint_models`, which `ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.advertisesCapability` fills per exact build. It also lists the structured forced-tool catalog builds with their model_types and parsers, and says GPT-OSS has no forced strategy and is not listed.

The text also says `NativeToolStreamRouter` drops ASCII framing whitespace around and between call frames in forced mode. Whitespace alone is still a missing call, and any other visible text is a 422 tool_choice violation. These statements are consistent with fail-closed validation and do not weaken T-007 or T-008. They affect output correctness and routing, not confidentiality (A-001) or the TB-002 encryption path.

The provider-side claims depend on code outside this batch: ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.swift, NativeToolStreamRouter and ToolConstraintValidation.validate. I did not verify them, and the coordinator-side routing is platform-owned and also unverified here. If a later pass reviews those source files, it should confirm that the exact-build `model_type` match is enforced and that non-ASCII whitespace is rejected as documented. The other lines in the supplied excerpts (Nemotron, Flint, prefix cache, SSD tier) are unchanged context. The documented prefix-cache posture is consistent with T-041, with no change to TTL, HMAC naming or scope. needs_deeper_review is false for this PR itself because the change is documentation only.
